items.t: (Yonhap Interview) New Italian trade commissioner sees K-food as gateway to broader bilateral trade
sum: SEOUL, Nov. 7 (Yonhap) -- The new commissioner at the Seoul office of the Italian Trade Agency (ITA) said K-food could help open the door to broader trade ties between South Korea and Italy, particularly in the wine sector.

"We plan to focus more on the wine sector, which is such an important part of Italian culture," Raimondo Lucariello said in a recent interview with Yonhap News Agency on Thursday, as the ITA marks the 100th anniversary of its founding.

Praising the popularity of Korean food globally and the country's vibrant cuisine scene, Lucariello said the agency plans to offer more wine-tasting classes tailored to South Koreans, whom he described as "great drinkers of soju," referring to the country's traditional distilled liquor.
He also pointed to the global popularity of Korean movies and music, saying Italy has much to learn from South Korea's success in promoting its cultural content internationally.
The ITA is a public agency tasked with supporting Italian companies in expanding their presence in overseas markets and promoting Italian products and businesses abroad.
High Street Italia, the agency's permanent Made in Italy promotional showroom and lifestyle complex located in southern Seoul, is a key part of such efforts.
It is the only showroom of its kind operated by the ITA worldwide, except for a similar yet smaller facility in Taipei opened just two months ago.

South Korea's KOSPI Plunges More Than 5% for Second Day, but Kakao and Naver Surge Around 10% as Money Rotates Into Platforms and Biotech
sum: Even in a rout that sent South Korea's KOSPI down more than 5% for a second consecutive session, buying piled into non-semiconductor sectors such as platforms, biotech and automakers, producing stocks with double-digit gains. As the semiconductor and AI infrastructure value chain took a direct hit from U.S.-driven regulatory worries, money rotated into sectors that had been overlooked.

An analysis of Korea Exchange data on Nov. 6 showed that of the 805 common stocks traded on the main board the previous day, when the KOSPI fell 5.28%, 302 (37.5%) closed higher. Decliners numbered 475 (59.0%), with 28 (3.5%) unchanged. That means that despite the index's sharp drop, a considerable number of individual stocks rose.

Platform stocks drew the most attention. Kakao climbed 10.65% and Naver gained 8.26%. Foreign investors net bought 71.4 billion won (approximately $52.6 million) worth of Naver, making it the top foreign net-buy that day, while institutions bought 54.3 billion won (approximately $40.0 million) worth. Kakao also saw foreign and institutional net buying of 26.6 billion won (approximately $19.6 million) and 19.6 billion won (approximately $14.4 million), respectively. The buying appears to be money that exited semiconductor stocks and flowed into platform names.

For Kakao, the announcement of shareholder return measures and third-quarter results served as catalysts. Kakao's board met the previous day and filed a corrected disclosure of its spin-off plan, adjusting the schedule and ratio. Under the revised plan, an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve the split will be held on Jan. 15 next year, and the spin-off date is set for Feb. 1, 2027. Third-quarter revenue was 2.0867 trillion won (approximately $1.5 billion) and operating profit was 240.3 billion won (approximately $176.9 million), up 6.3% and 7.4% respectively from a year earlier, in line with market expectations.

Institutional money also flowed into large pharmaceutical and biotech names. Celltrion rose 7.50%, with trading value of 428 billion won (approximately $315.0 million), the highest among gainers. Institutions net bought 223.3 billion won (approximately $164.4 million) worth of Celltrion, their second-largest purchase after SK Hynix.

S. Korean won nudges lower against U.S. dollar on foreign outflows
sum: SEOUL, Nov. 5 (Yonhap) -- The South Korean won nudged lower against the U.S. dollar Thursday, as offshore investors remained net sellers of local stocks after a Democratic Party win in the U.S. midterm elections.
The won was quoted at 1,342.1 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 0.6 won from the close of the previous stock trading session.

With Democrats winning majorities in both the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, traders have expected it to weaken the power of U.S. President Donald Trump during the final two years of his term.
For the local semiconductor industry, one of the key things to watch going forward is whether a Democrat-controlled Congress would slow the pace of building data centers for artificial intelligence.

Foreign investors sold a net 3.39 trillion won (US$2.53 billion) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index plunging 5.28 percent to close at 5,383.80.

Seoul shares close higher on early U.S. midterm election outcome
sum: SEOUL, Nov. 4 (Yonhap) -- South Korean stocks closed slightly higher Wednesday as early results from the U.S. midterm elections pointed to Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress. The local currency was trading lower against the U.S. dollar.
Swinging between gains and losses, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) finished at 5,683.80, up 35.01 points, or 0.62 percent.

After starting 2.43 percent higher, the KOSPI turned lower around 10:11 a.m. and fell as low as 5,421.72 at 12:45 p.m. as vote counting in the U.S. midterm elections progressed, before narrowing its losses and turning positive in the afternoon.

Early results pointed to Democrats regaining control of both the Senate and the House, raising the prospect of changes to key policies of the Trump administration, including tighter regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and support for renewable energy and secondary batteries.

sum: SEOUL, Nov. 3 (Yonhap) -- South Korean stocks traded more than 2 percent lower late Tuesday morning, led by tech losses amid lingering woes about the excessive pace of artificial intelligence (AI) spending.
Opening 2.46 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 145.02 points, or 2.48 percent, to 5,714.06 as of 11:20 a.m.
Overnight on Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 closed 1.07 percent and 0.51 percent lower, respectively, ahead of the U.S. midterm elections slated for Tuesday.
Investor sentiment was dampened by concerns that massive spending on AI infrastructure is undermining tech firms' near-term profitability.
Market bellwether Samsung Electronics sank 2.95 percent, and its chipmaking rival SK hynix slid 3.8 percent.
Hanmi Semiconductor, a leading chip equipment maker, fell 4.17 percent, and SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, tumbled 4 percent.
Steel giant POSCO Holdings slumped 5.3 percent, and leading oil refinery SK Innovation plunged 7.76 percent.

Siemens stock gains as Naver talks spotlight industrial AI
sum: Siemens stock traded at 268.08 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:35 CET on Monday, November 2, 0.91 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The move came as fresh industrial AI discussions added a strategic technology angle ahead of Siemens' next corporate update.

The Herald Business reported on Monday that Siemens Group Chairman Roland Busch and Naver CEO Choi Soo-yeon held a dialogue on industrial AI at the Asia-Pacific German Business Conference in Seoul on Saturday, October 31. The talks focused on combining German engineering with Asian strengths in AI, chips and digital platforms across manufacturing, energy and mobility.

Choi said industrial AI would reach a true tipping point only when small and midsize companies and their suppliers could use it with ease. She also stressed that human oversight becomes more important as AI handles a wider range of tasks. The comments frame adoption as a supply-chain and productivity issue rather than only a software feature.

Busch said industrial AI would create its full value only when deployed safely and reliably in the field and scaled across industries. That emphasis is relevant for Siemens because the group's industrial offering combines automation, software and digital-twin capabilities with applications in physical production environments.

After the dialogue, Siemens executives visited Naver's 1784 headquarters. The companies discussed cases in which Naver's digital-twin technology has been used in industrial settings and explored ways to take those applications into global markets alongside Siemens' industrial solutions. They also considered cooperation involving robotics and robot foundation models.

The discussions build on a June memorandum of understanding between Naver Cloud and Korea Siemens to advance AI transformation in manufacturing. The planned cooperation combines Siemens industrial automation and digital-twin technology with Naver Cloud's AI and cloud infrastructure, while also targeting joint customer development and industry-specific projects.
For investors, the talks reinforce Siemens' positioning in industrial AI but do not by themselves establish additional revenue or earnings.

Naver shares in freefall as Nvidia investment fails to lift stock
sum: Naver's share price has been plunging to historic lows even as positive news continues to emerge. When Nvidia's $1 billion investment in the company was confirmed Friday, the stock still tumbled to 165,000 won during trading — a sign that even major good news cannot arrest the decline.
After the announcement, Naver shares rose 4.13 percent in after-hours trading Saturday, but fell even further when regular trading resumed.
Naver said Nvidia will invest $1 billion in the company on Friday, becoming its third-largest shareholder.

Earlier, Naver signed a new share subscription agreement with Nvidia on July 24 and decided to issue new shares through a third-party allotment. At the time, Nvidia set a condition requiring Naver to secure at least $9 billion worth of computing infrastructure for AI factory expansion, separate from the $1 billion investment. Naver recently signed a related agreement with Brookfield, satisfying that prerequisite.
"Much of the concern that had been raised about whether Naver's business would proceed will be substantially resolved," said Ahn Jae-min, an analyst at NH Investment & Securities.

Shareholders who had hoped the confirmed Nvidia investment would lift the stock were left stunned. The share price, which had topped 300,000 won earlier this year, has collapsed to near historic lows. Many investors are said to have bought Naver shares at peak prices between 280,000 and 300,000 won, leaving a significant number sitting on losses of roughly 50 percent.
"I thought the share price would go up, but it fell even further," one Naver shareholder said.

Google Chrome Logs 260 Million Hours to Lead Naver in Korea
sum: Google Chrome logged 260 million hours of mobile usage in South Korea in September, extending its lead over local portal Naver for the fifth consecutive month.
Chrome held the top spot after outpacing Naver’s 240 million hours during the month, according to mobile app analytics firm Wiseapp Retail.

Samsung Internet took third place with 130 million hours. Together, the top three applications generated 630 million hours, accounting for about 80 percent of total usage time among the country’s 10 most-used search and browser apps.
Google’s search app came fourth with 87 million hours, followed by Brave with 38 million hours and Daum with 23 million hours.
Whale recorded 5.7 million hours, while Nate and Firefox each logged 3.5 million hours. Microsoft Edge rounded out the top 10 with 1.8 million hours.

For brands and digital retailers in South Korea, the continued shift away from Naver’s integrated ecosystem toward Chrome reshapes consumer discovery pathways. Naver built its commercial engine by bundling search results directly with its own shopping comparison engine, smart stores, and payment rails. When shoppers conduct queries directly in a web browser rather than inside Naver’s walled garden, default search engine settings and standard web indexing dilute that proprietary checkout loop.

Google’s expanding footprint also splits consumer attention between dedicated mobile apps and direct web links. Retailers that previously focused technical resources exclusively on Naver SEO and proprietary storefronts now face higher ad spending requirements to capture high-intent buyers across multiple independent search feeds.

items.t: SK Hynix Stocks Rise With 30% Efficiency Claim in New Memory
sum: SK hynix, the memory-chip and AI-server component supplier SKHY, presents another way to sell memory into AI infrastructure: shared capacity across servers. Its Korean shares closed at ?1,272,000, up 0.79% on October 16. The pitch goes beyond high-bandwidth memory. More types of memory inside each AI installation could give the company more products to sell.

In its October 16 disclosure, SK hynix described a 256-gigabyte CXL 3.2 module delivering 80 gigabytes per second of bandwidth, with roughly 30% better energy efficiency than its predecessor, according to the company. It also outlined proof-of-concept work with NAVER Cloud to share cached AI data. That is a technical milestone. It does not establish a volume order, a shipment schedule or a revenue contribution.

The GF Score of 76/100 shows strong growth, profitability and financial strength readings, alongside a sharply weaker momentum reading. That gives investors useful context, but it does not settle the commercial question. A successful demonstration still needs to turn into customer qualifications and paying orders. Shared memory could help customers squeeze more work from their servers; the payoff for SK hynix depends on how many modules they buy and the margins those sales deliver.

sum: The 7.6-percent crash on Thursday extended the KOSPI’s losses to over 20 percent across seven consecutive sessions, leaving investors who borrowed to chase the rally facing pressure to put up more collateral or sell.

For Jang, a company employee in his 30s working in Seoul’s Seongsu-dong district, can't find words to describe his state of mind. The SK hynix shares he bought at 2.5 million won apiece were trading at roughly half that price.
"I’ve deleted the trading app,” he said. “If I look on, I think I'll get a heart attack."
The KOSPI, once the envy of global markets after doubling from the start of the year to approach 10,000 in June, ended at 5,554.22 — little more than half its June level.
The KOSDAQ also tumbled 7.65 percent to 760.82. Both markets triggered sell-side “sidecars,” temporarily suspending program sell orders.

Semiconductor heavyweights led the decline. SK hynix plunged more than 11 percent and Samsung Electronics lost 9.5 percent as higher-than-expected U.S. inflation and doubts over returns on artificial intelligence investment weighed on technology shares.
“Can’t the Korean stock market just take a week off?” one user wrote on Naver’s stock discussion board.

Kurly revisits IPO as profits improve, Naver backing grows
sum: Online grocery platform continues talks with underwriters, but valuation concerns and listing timeline remain uncertain

Online Korean grocery platform Kurly is reviving plans for an initial public offering as improving profitability and a partnership with Naver strengthen its valuation prospects, potentially opening an exit route for long-standing investors.

According to market sources Wednesday, Kurly has been holding regular discussions with its IPO underwriters — Korea Investment & Securities, NH Investment & Securities and JPMorgan — over a possible listing.
"We continue to hold regular meetings with our underwriters, but our focus remains on improving performance and enhancing our valuation," a Kurly official said.

The renewed IPO prospects follow a turnaround in earnings. Kurly posted revenue of 2.37 trillion won ($1.7 billion) and operating profit of 13.1 billion won last year, achieving its first annual operating profit since its founding.

Momentum has continued this year. In the first half, the company recorded revenue of 1.08 trillion won, operating profit of 51.6 billion won and net profit of 45.7 billion won. Its six-month operating profit was nearly four times its full-year figure for 2025, while it also swung to a net profit.

Kurly previously pursued an IPO after securing a valuation of around 4 trillion won in a 2021 pre-IPO funding round, but shelved the plan in 2023 amid deteriorating market conditions and a declining valuation.

Naver Z workers strike to oppose wage freeze, press CEO Kim Chang-uk
sum: The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) Korean Chemical, Textile & Food Workers' Union (KCTFU) Naver chapter said Naver Z union members began a one-day all-out strike on the 23rd. Naver Z is the operator of the Metaverse platform "Zepeto."

According to the union, about 120 Naver Z members, or roughly 70%, are taking part in the all-out strike that day. The union said members plan to join a YouTube live stream from 10 a.m. for 30 minutes and argue that management is shifting responsibility for worsening business conditions onto employees by freezing wages.

The union also held a four-hour partial strike on the 9th to urge management to take a more forward-leaning stance in the 2026 wage negotiations. At the time, the union demanded the withdrawal of the unilateral wage freeze, a 5.3% wage increase, and a responsible explanation from Naver Z CEO Kim Chang-uk about the business situation. However, the union said that in the two weeks after the partial strike, management provided no response to the demands for a wage increase and an explanation from executives.

The union specifically claimed that after CEO Kim Chang-uk took sole charge of the Zepeto service, companywide town hall meetings were held only twice, in April 2024 and February 2025. Accordingly, the union argued that management froze wages citing a management crisis without sufficiently explaining the service's direction and vision or communicating with employees. Kim concurrently serves as co-CEO of four key Naver subsidiaries and affiliates: Snow, Naver Z, Kream, and Cake. Among them, Naver Z and Cake have frozen employee annual salaries this year.

Oh Se-yun, head of the Naver chapter, said, "A culture of wielding authority without taking responsibility keeps repeating at Naver," adding, "In normal times they do not share authority with employees, and when the company struggles, they shift the cause and responsibility onto employees." He continued, "Our demand to withdraw the salary freeze and hold a decisive debate with CEO Kim Chang-uk on Jet's future still stands," adding, "After the Chuseok holiday ends, we will send an open inquiry to CEO Kim Chang-uk and Chair Lee Hae-jin."

Kiwoom Securities Introduces Cross-Trading System for Unlisted Stocks... Partners with Naver Pay
sum: Kiwoom Securities is creating a more accessible environment for unlisted stock trading.

On September 22, Kiwoom Securities announced that it had signed a business agreement with Naver Pay Unlisted (Npay Unlisted), an unlisted stock trading platform, for the introduction of a cross-trading system for unlisted stocks.

Previously, Naver Pay Unlisted only allowed transactions between buyers and sellers who held accounts with the same securities firm. With the introduction of the cross-trading system, Kiwoom Securities customers will be able to freely trade on Naver Pay Unlisted using their existing accounts, without having to open a separate account.

Cross-trading enhances investor convenience. As customers from various securities firms gather on a single platform, the liquidity of the over-the-counter (OTC) stock market increases. This also facilitates a virtuous cycle of productive finance, allowing funds to flow more smoothly into ventures and startups.

Starting with this agreement, Kiwoom Securities plans to seamlessly integrate cross-trading infrastructure. The two companies will continue their collaboration to provide a simpler and more convenient investment environment for unlisted stocks in the future.

Lee Youngmin, CEO of Naver Pay Unlisted, stated, "By leveraging the expertise and capabilities of Kiwoom Securities, we will expand cooperation to institutionalize and vitalize the OTC market for unlisted stocks. We aim to contribute to creating a healthy investment environment for unlisted stocks by connecting investors with promising unlisted companies more effectively."

Naver's KRW 14 Trillion, 1GW AI Factory Deal Redraws Its Valuation Formula
sum: This infographic, originally published by Korea Financial Times, has been reconstructed using generative AI.

According to industry sources on August 20, the business value of Naver's AI Factory operations is estimated at KRW 14.4 trillion — up KRW 3.3 trillion in about two months from the KRW 11.1 trillion valuation calculated in June, when Naver first entered the AI Factory business.

Naver's AI Factory goes beyond simply leasing data center space, integrating GPU and computing resources into a unified offering. Attention is focused on whether Naver can convert years of technology investment in AI and its data center operating experience into a reliable cash cow.

Kim Jin-gu, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities, said AI Factory operations account for roughly 30% of Naver's total estimated corporate value of KRW 48.7 trillion. He added that if Naver makes strategic decisions for the mid-to-long-term growth of its core businesses through robust cooperation with global frontier companies, there is room for the company's valuation to rise further from current levels.

The estimated business value of the AI Factory unit already far exceeds the KRW 7.3 trillion combined valuation of Naver's existing core businesses, including its search platform and cloud operations.

Naver continues to post steady results in both the B2C and B2B segments of its AI business. On the B2C side, the company unveiled Korea's first hyperscale AI model, HyperCLOVA, in 2021 and has since applied it across its services to strengthen its platform competitiveness.

Naver's platform division posted revenue of KRW 1.9022 trillion in the second quarter of this year, up 12.3% from a year earlier and 3.4% from the previous quarter. Advertising revenue grew 7.5% year-on-year, with AI contributing more than 60% of that growth on the back of AI-driven ad placement optimization and enhanced targeting. In particular, the AI Briefing ad product, which officially launched in late July, has recorded a click-through conversion rate more than 30% higher and a purchase conversion rate more than three times higher than existing search ads, demonstrating the monetization potential of generative AI services.

Alibaba Cloud opens third South Korea datacentre
sum: Alibaba Cloud has switched on its third datacentre in South Korea, a year after its second facility went live and four years after it first put infrastructure on the ground in the country.
The Chinese hyperscaler announced the launch on 18 August 2026 without disclosing the capacity of the new site, which takes its global network to 104 availability zones across 30 regions.

The facility will offer a suite of services, including compute, storage, networking, security, databases, containers and cloud-native services. With the launch, Alibaba Cloud is also bringing its agentic artificial intelligence (AI) portfolio to the market, among them agentic development, testing operations and security services to help enterprises manage the full lifecycle of an AI agent.

Yongjoon Yoon, country manager for South Korea at Alibaba Cloud Intelligence, said South Korea is a key market where Alibaba Cloud has continued to make long-term investments, adding that the third datacentre is an investment to help South Korean enterprises operate AI and cloud-based services more reliably and “not merely an infrastructure expansion”.

Gendive, an AI company based in Gwangju, has integrated Alibaba Cloud’s Wan video generation and HappyHorse image generation models into DevDive, its no-code platform for building and orchestrating business workflows.

Other local customers include Naver Z, the Naver subsidiary behind the Zepeto metaverse platform, which is running real-time 3D avatar generation and rendering on Alibaba Cloud infrastructure. The supplier also sells through local partners Megazone Soft and Team Sparta.

As for government workloads, Alibaba Cloud has not announced any compliance with Korea’s Cloud Security Assurance Program (CSAP), which requires suppliers serving government agencies to keep data, equipment and operations staff inside the country. For years, no foreign supplier cleared even the lowest tier of the CSAP certification until Microsoft broke through in November 2024, followed by Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services (AWS) in early 2025.

"NPS Sweeps Up This Stock After Selling 960 Billion Won"
sum: The National Pension Service (NPS) has recently overhauled its domestic stock portfolio through rebalancing, resulting in notable changes. While it injected over 1.5 trillion won into SK hynix, taking advantage of additional purchasing capacity following a price correction, it sold nearly 1 trillion won worth of shares in SK Square, which had previously benefited from the rise in SK hynix's share value.

According to the Korea Exchange on August 18, since the NPS began rebalancing on July 1 until August 14, SK hynix was the most heavily purchased stock by pension funds. During this period, the pension funds made net purchases of SK hynix shares worth 1.5339 trillion won.

Other stocks that ranked high in net purchases included SK Innovation (283.1 billion won), S-Oil (210.9 billion won), Celltrion (210.5 billion won), Naver (184.2 billion won), Samsung Biologics (156.8 billion won), DB Insurance (151.3 billion won), SK Telecom (150.9 billion won), and LG Electronics (141.4 billion won).

Conversely, the most heavily sold stock during the same period was SK Square. Pension funds made net sales of SK Square worth 964.6 billion won. Other significant net sales included Samsung Electronics (389.8 billion won), Samsung Electro-Mechanics (329 billion won), LG Innotek (175.4 billion won), Hyundai Motor Company (163.6 billion won), Hyundai Mobis (152.7 billion won), Samsung Life Insurance (146.8 billion won), Hanwha Ocean (125.1 billion won), and Mirae Asset Securities (112.1 billion won).

Because a substantial portion of the transactions categorized as pension fund trades by the Korea Exchange are executed by the NPS, these flows are largely interpreted as a reflection of the National Pension Service's portfolio adjustments.

Notably, there has been a visible movement of funds among SK Group stocks. Pension funds also made net sales of SK amounting to 55.9 billion won during the same period. The market attributes this to the correction in SK hynix's share price after the end of June. SK hynix, which had already surged considerably since last year, accounted for a significant share of the NPS's domestic equity portfolio, limiting further purchases. However, the price correction created opportunities for direct purchasing.

sum: Naver announced on the 7th that its revenue for the second quarter of this year increased by 16.2% year-on-year to 3.3888 trillion won. Operating profit was 520.3 billion won, a slight decrease of 0.2% compared to the same period last year. Net income attributable to owners of the parent company reached 704.3 billion won, up 41.6% from the same period last year.

Revenue grew by double digits as AI integration expanded in core businesses such as advertising and commerce, while the global C2C (consumer-to-consumer) business also saw growth. However, operating profit declined slightly due to massive investments in AI infrastructure.
Revenue by segment: △Naver Platform 1.9022 trillion won △Financial Platform 470.7 billion won △Global Challenge 1.0159 trillion won.

Naver Platform revenue increased by 12.3% year-on-year and 3.4% quarter-on-quarter. Among these, advertising revenue rose by 7.5% compared to the same period last year. AI's contribution to revenue growth through AI-based content optimization and advanced targeting exceeded 60%. Notably, the AI briefing ad, officially launched at the end of July, showed a click-through rate 30% higher and a purchase conversion rate three times higher than existing search ads. Service revenue increased by 31.3% year-on-year.

Financial Platform revenue grew by 16.0% year-on-year and 2.4% quarter-on-quarter. Npay payment volume in the second quarter reached 25.2 trillion won, up 21.0% from the same period last year, driven by Smart Store's growth and expansion of its external ecosystem. Naver demonstrated rapid expansion in the AI platform business for businesses through the offline-online integrated terminal 'Npay Connect'. Naver plans to integrate online and offline data to enhance its ecosystem competitiveness.

The Global Challenge segment increased by 24.4% year-on-year and 7.9% quarter-on-quarter, with the C2C business driving revenue growth. C2C transaction volume and revenue rose by 74.9% year-on-year and 13.3% quarter-on-quarter, respectively, due to strengthened competitiveness in platforms such as Walapop, Poshmark, and Soda. Content revenue increased by 0.5% year-on-year and 5.5% quarter-on-quarter.

sum: Korean stocks traded nearly 13 percent higher late Friday morning as investors scooped up semiconductor shares following Microsoft's strong earnings.
After opening 1.15 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) expanded its gains, adding 717.3 points, or 12.82 percent, to trade at 6,310.86 as of 11:20 a.m.
The surge followed a three-session heavy sell-off due mainly to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending. The KOSPI fell nearly 40 percent this month alone.
Overnight, Wall Street closed higher as Microsoft's stronger-than-expected earnings report eased fears about massive spending on AI infrastructure.

The S&P 500 climbed 1.66 percent and the Nasdaq gained 2.78 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.19 percent. The PHLX chip index, a gauge of U.S. semiconductor giants, surged 8.2 percent.
In Seoul, market bellwether Samsung Electronics shot up 18.24 percent, and SK hynix skyrocketed 21.86 percent.
Top carmaker Hyundai Motor jumped 6.98 percent, and internet firm Naver gained 5.03 percent.

items.t: Nvidia invests US$1B in Naver's sovereign AI push
sum: Nvidia plans to invest in South Korean internet and cloud giant Naver through a US$1 billion third-party share issue for about a 4.5% stake, a move that could make it Naver's third-largest shareholder if the deal closes and treasury shares are canceled. The two companies are also teaming up with global investment firm Brookfield on an AI infrastructure plan worth as much as US$10 billion to turn Naver's GAK Sejong data center into the core of South Korea's sovereign AI factory initiative.

items.s: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
sum: Naver announced on July 27 that it will conduct a third-party allotment share issuance worth $1 billion to Nvidia Corp., according to a regulatory filing released the same day.
Under the transaction, Naver will issue 7,241,564 new common shares, giving Nvidia a 4.5% stake upon completion. Payment for the subscription is scheduled for Oct. 30.

The equity investment builds on a June agreement between Naver and Nvidia to jointly develop gigawatt-scale global artificial intelligence (AI) factories, positioning Nvidia as both a shareholder and strategic partner in Naver’s AI infrastructure operations.

Separately, Naver named Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. as its exclusive capital partner for AI infrastructure financing of up to $9 billion. Brookfield manages more than $1 trillion in assets across sectors including data centers, power, and renewable energy.
The proposed $9 billion financing with Brookfield remains subject to final agreement, with definitive investment commitments and terms to be determined through ongoing negotiations.

Combining Brookfield’s capital backing and Nvidia’s technology platform, Naver plans to expand its AI factory operations centered on GAK Sejong, its hyperscale data center in Sejong City. The company targets expanding AI factory capacity to 200 megawatts (MW) by 2028 and scaling to 1 gigawatt (GW) over the longer term. The facilities will incorporate Nvidia's Blackwell platform and its next-generation Vera Rubin platform.

Naver plans to launch a 55MW AI factory in the first half of 2027 to begin generating revenue, before expanding to 200MW starting in 2028. It will then target demand for sovereign AI infrastructure across South Korea, the United States, the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, and the Middle East.

sum: - Separately, a Wall Street Journal report said that Nvidia was in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI as part of a massive data-center project.

Nvidia Corp. shares rose 1% in overnight trading late Sunday amid a slew of partnership news, which appears to be injecting fresh optimism in the key AI stock that has curiously lagged chip peers this year.

Nvidia is investing $1 billion in Naver, known as South Korea's Google, to help finance a new data center in the country that is sponsored by U.S. private equity firm Brookfield, according to an announcement late Friday. The data center will use Nvidia's AI accelerators.
Nvidia is also teaming up with SK Group to build more than 2 gigawatts of AI data centers on the Korean Peninsula. The first of those is being built by SK Telecom and will open next year.

The development signals Nvidia's expanding presence in the Asian country, home to two of the world's largest chipmakers, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. For Nvidia, closer ties with SK Group will help improve its access to computer memory chips.

Chairman Lee Hae-jin Announces Major Partnership with NVIDIA and Brookfield to Jointly Build an AI Factory
sum: NAVER and NVIDIA’s gigawatt (GW)-scale AI factory agreement, announced last June, took concrete shape through two contracts signed in July. On July 22, NAVER signed a preliminary agreement worth $9 billion with global investment firm Brookfield, and on the 24th, signed a strategic investment agreement worth $1 billion with NVIDIA. That same afternoon, at the AI Summit in San Francisco, NAVER Board Chairman Lee Hae-jin shared the background and significance of this partnership.

As global demand for AI surges, competition to secure the large-scale computing resources needed for AI model development and service operation – so-called “AI factories” – is intensifying. An AI factory is a new form of AI infrastructure that combines GPU computing resources with networking, storage, power and cooling systems, and software platforms into a single unit.

NAVER recognized the value of data centers early on and has continued to invest aggressively. It became the first Korean IT company to build its own self-designed data centers – “GAK Chuncheon” (2013) and “GAK Sejong” (2023) – and has directly operated every layer of the AI factory stack, from data centers and GPU clusters to AI platforms, its own models, and services.

NAVER is the only company in Korea that provides large-scale GPUaaS (GPU-as-a-Service), and is recognized as one of the few companies in the world capable of leading a sovereign AI business. For NAVER, this partnership will be a decisive opportunity to expand that capability onto the global stage.
Backed by NVIDIA’s $1 billion strategic investment and $9 billion in AI infrastructure assets to be raised by Brookfield, NAVER will build a $10 billion AI factory.

The AI factory will run on NVIDIA’s optimized platform, the “DSX Architecture,” with the latest Blackwell GPU platform and the next-generation Vera Rubin platform to be introduced in phases. Once the definitive agreement with the preferred bidder is signed, Brookfield will raise up to $9 billion through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) to fund the capital and infrastructure needed to build the AI factory.

To further strengthen this partnership, NVIDIA has decided to participate in NAVER’s third-party private placement of new shares worth approximately $1 billion – the first such investment by NVIDIA in Asia.

Naver Surges 10% on Brookfield AI Talks as Asian Chipmakers Rally on Alphabet Capex Boom
sum: Naver Corp. shares surged nearly 10% on Wednesday, reclaiming the ₩210,000 level, as investors piled in on expectations that a visit by top executives to Brookfield Asset Management’s Toronto headquarters could unlock a multi-trillion-won artificial intelligence infrastructure deal. The rally in Seoul dovetailed with a broader advance across Asian equity markets, where chipmakers led gains after Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) unveiled a massive increase in capital spending that underscored the relentless buildout of AI infrastructure.

Naver’s stock jumped as much as 9.69% to ₩215,000, clawing back a significant portion of recent losses driven by concerns over rising AI investment costs and downward revisions to earnings estimates. The sharp move higher was fueled by market chatter that Naver founder and board chairman Lee Hae-jin, CEO Choi Soo-yeon, and CFO Kim Hee-chul traveled to Canada this week to meet with Brookfield, a global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion in assets under management. The presence of the CFO, who oversees financing strategy, signaled to investors that the discussions likely went beyond casual business development and touched on the capital structure and funding mechanisms required to build a so-called AI factory.

Naver has been working with Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) on a long-term plan to construct a gigawatt-scale global AI factory. The roadmap envisions an initial 55-megawatt facility coming online in the first half of next year, scaling to 100 megawatts including overseas sites, and eventually reaching 200 megawatts by 2028. The enormous capital requirements for such a project — which integrates massive GPU clusters, high-speed networking, power supply, and cooling infrastructure — have weighed on investor sentiment. A partnership with Brookfield, which last year launched a program with Nvidia and the Kuwait Investment Authority targeting up to $100 billion in AI infrastructure investments, would materially ease the financial burden on Naver’s balance sheet and transform the project from a cost center into a capital-efficient growth engine.

items.t: Seoul stocks erase early losses late Tues. morning on bargain hunting
sum: SEOUL July 21 (Yonhap) -- Seoul stocks erased earlier losses and were trading higher late Tuesday morning as investors went bargain hunting for technology stocks.
The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) changed its trajectory, going up 149.39 points, or 2.29 percent, to 6,665.66, as of 11:25 a.m.
Foreign and institutional investors lifted the index as they snatched up tech heavyweights.
Overnight U.S. stocks closed lower as investors weighed the risk of renewed hostilities in the Middle East, with upcoming earnings reports from major tech companies later this week.

The United States has completed more strikes against Iran, the U.S. Central Command said later Monday (local time), hours after President Donald Trump said Iran would pay for the deaths of three service members.
Chip giant Samsung Electronics added 4.82 percent, while its industry rival SK hynix advanced 2.72 percent.
Major financial firm KB Financial inched up 0.3 percent, defense giant Hanwha Aerospace moved up 2.63 percent, and portal operator Naver rose 3.17 percent.

Backlash over leveraged chip ETFs persists despite tighter rules
sum: "Why are they penalizing only retail investors? If regulators can't fix the problem, they should just delist these products. They're wreaking havoc on the market," one user recently wrote on a Naver stock investing community.
"I've lost nearly 60 percent investing in these leveraged ETFs (exchange-traded funds) myself, but these measures won't do anything to restore order to the market," another wrote.

The comments reflect mounting frustration among retail investors after financial authorities last Thursday tightened trading rules for single-stock leveraged ETFs tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

The newly announced measures raised the minimum deposit requirement to 30 million won ($20,200) from 10 million won, and required investors to fully fund purchases in cash. Previously, investors could meet up to 70 percent of the 10 million won deposit requirement with the value of stocks they already owned.
Regulators also agreed to temporarily halt new product launches, ban advertising for existing products and raise the minimum order size to 20 units from one until market conditions stabilize.
Many investors, however, argue the restrictions fail to properly address concerns that the products amplify market volatility.
Since their launch in May, the 16 products have attracted more than 13 trillion won in trading value, fueled by strong retail demand for amplified exposure to Korea's two largest chipmakers.

items.t: Naver locks in $10B from Brookfield and Nvidia for AI data center push
NH Investment Says Naver’s Post-AI Data Center Plunge Is Overdone, Keeps ₩320,000 Target
sum: Naver’s stock has plummeted more than 30% in a single month since the company announced plans to build a 1GW artificial intelligence data center in partnership with Nvidia, but analysts at NH Investment & Securities believe the sell-off is overdone.

On the 9th, NH Investment & Securities maintained its ‘buy’ rating on Naver and a target price of 320,000 won (approximately $212.51), representing roughly 66% upside from the previous day’s closing price of 192,700 won. The firm’s view is that market concerns over AI investment have been excessively reflected in the share price.

“The 1GW data center investment is positive because it allows us to anticipate performance in the business-to-business (B2B) AI market, centered on the Neo Cloud business,” said Ahn Jae-min, an analyst at NH Investment & Securities. “Once data center-related revenue begins to materialize after 2027, the positive impact will likely outweigh the concerns.”

Naver previously announced it would enter the AI factory business in cooperation with Nvidia, building a total of 1GW of AI data center capacity. The strategy marks a shift away from its business-to-consumer (B2C) structure, expanding into the B2B sector by constructing and leasing AI data centers to large enterprises. However, the market reaction was chilly. While data center-related revenue is not expected to ramp up until after 2027, GPU investments alone this year are projected to reach approximately 1 trillion won (approximately $664.1 million), fueling worries about the cost burden. The stock, which had climbed to 288,500 won at the time of the announcement, has since fallen more than 30% over the past month.

“Building a 1GW data center requires 60 trillion to 70 trillion won (approximately $39.8 billion to approximately $46.5 billion), but if annual revenue reaches around 20 trillion won (approximately $13.3 billion) after completion, the data center’s value is estimated at roughly 13 trillion won (approximately $8.6 billion),” Ahn analyzed. “The stock price decline following the announcement is excessive.”

Naver’s second-quarter results are estimated to show revenue of 3.35 trillion won (approximately $2.2 billion), up 15% year-on-year, and operating profit of 550 billion won (approximately $365.3 million), an increase in the 5% range.

"How a 135-won stock became worth 2.9 million won" ... The full story of the Hynix myth [Issue Plus]
sum: Artificial intelligence is reshaping the flow of capital around the world. At the center of that shift is High Bandwidth Memory. It is an essential semiconductor for training large language models, running data centers, and powering AI accelerators. SK hynix has led the HBM market. NVIDIA has adopted this memory for its AI chips.

The AI boom has become a boom for SK hynix. After posting 47 trillion won in operating profit in 2025, the company recorded 37.6103 trillion won in operating profit in the first quarter of 2026 alone. Its operating margin reached 72 percent. That is an unprecedented, dreamlike figure in semiconductor history. The stock price, which was in the 26,000-won range in 2016, climbed above 2.9 million won in 2026.

Analysts say this semiconductor supercycle is different from previous ones. In the past, supercycles were tied to PC and smartphone replacement cycles. This time, demand is driven by AI. AI models constantly consume high-performance memory during training, inference, and service operations.

Maeil Business Plus, Maeil Business Newspaper's premium wealth-management platform, has compiled a comprehensive profile of SK hynix, now at the center of the global AI industry. Based on the annual report filed on March 17, 2026, for fiscal year 78, and the quarterly report submitted on May 15, 2026, for the first quarter of fiscal year 79, it also analyzed SK hynix's official newsroom, official website, the Maeil Business Newspaper database, and other sources to organize 100 facts. The foundation is not stock forecasts or rumors, but the numbers the company itself disclosed and official records.
Who owns SK hynix, who is shaping it, how much does it earn, and where does it invest?

By following the company's path, readers can sharpen their eye for identifying firms that may be struggling now but have the potential to grow into global leaders. SK hynix's direction and goals also offer a glimpse into the future of the Korean economy and the global semiconductor industry.

In 1949, a construction company calledKukdo Constructionwas founded in Icheon, Gyeonggi Province. The company's more than 1 million pyeong of land in Icheon would later become the heart of South Korea's semiconductor industry.
